equation: dX = Y dt;  dY = -X dt + sigma dW(t)
milstein_correction: 0 (additive noise, Milstein == EM). Also multi-D, so Milstein not applicable.
implementation_notes: 2D linear stochastic harmonic oscillator with additive noise entering only the Y component: G = [[0], [sigma]]. State X has shape (num_paths, 2). Update: X_{n+1} = X_n + Y_n*dt (no noise); Y_{n+1} = Y_n - X_n*dt + sigma*dW_n. Use Euler-Maruyama (additive noise + multi-D, so Milstein is neither needed nor well-defined). Long horizon T = 10*pi (five full periods) accumulates phase error in the mean and variance growth, so a small dt is required for stability and accuracy (e.g. dt <= 0.001 or an order-preserving scheme). At T = 10*pi: mean_X = cos(10*pi) = 1.0, mean_Y = -sin(10*pi) = 0.0 (near zero -> skip mean check for Y). Analytic per-component moment formulas from sde_manual.md hold for any t and are evaluated at t = T.
